modules.title: Addition of angular momenta
modules.doc:
Couples two angular momenta and identifies the total angular momentum on the
Clebsch–Gordan decomposition.

## i. Overview

Two angular momentum representations on `V` and `W` give one on `V ⊗ W`, with total angular
momentum `J = J₁ ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ J₂`. The standard module `V(n)` carries the spin-`n/2`
representation with `Jz = H/2`, `J+ = E` and `J- = F`. For spins `j₁ = m/2` and `j₂ = n/2` the
total `J²` acts on the `k`-th lowering string of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` by `J(J + 1)` with
`J = j₁ + j₂ - k`, and `Jz` acts on its `l`-th vector by `J - l`. As `k` runs from `0` to
`min m n`, `J` runs from `j₁ + j₂` down to `|j₁ - j₂|`. The Clebsch–Gordan equivalence
`cgEquiv` intertwines `Jz`, `J+` and `J-` of the coupled system with those of the spin-`J`
representations on the summands.

## ii. Key results

- `AngularMomentumRepresentation.tensor` is the coupled representation on `V ⊗ W`.
- `AngularMomentumRepresentation.standard` is the spin-`n/2` representation on `V(n)`.
- `Jsq_coupled_stringVec` and `Jz_coupled_stringVec` give the total `J²` and `Jz` on the
  lowering strings.
- `cgEquiv_Jz_coupled`, `cgEquiv_Jp_coupled` and `cgEquiv_Jm_coupled` give the intertwining
  with the summands.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Coupled angular momentum
- B. The spin-`n/2` representation on `V(n)`
- C. Total angular momentum on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`
  - C.1. Eigenvalues on the lowering strings
  - C.2. Intertwining with the summands

## iv. References

- Mathlib, `Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.Sl2`.

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.tensor
declarations.doc: The coupled angular momentum `J = J₁ ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ J₂` on `V ⊗ W`.
declarations.statement:
def tensor (ρ₁ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (ρ₂ : AngularMomentumRepresentation W) :
    AngularMomentumRepresentation (V ⊗[ℂ] W)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.tensor_Jp
declarations.statement:
lemma tensor_Jp (ρ₁ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (ρ₂ : AngularMomentumRepresentation W) :
    (tensor ρ₁ ρ₂).Jp = diagEnd ρ₁.Jp ρ₂.Jp

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.tensor_Jm
declarations.statement:
lemma tensor_Jm (ρ₁ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (ρ₂ : AngularMomentumRepresentation W) :
    (tensor ρ₁ ρ₂).Jm = diagEnd ρ₁.Jm ρ₂.Jm

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.ρE_mul_ρF
declarations.doc: `EF = FE + H` on `V(n)`, the associative form of `⁅E, F⁆ = H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ρE_mul_ρF :
    (ρE : Module.End ℂ (StandardSl2Module ℂ n)) * ρF = ρF * ρE + ρH

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.ρH_mul_ρE
declarations.doc: `HE = EH + 2E` on `V(n)`, the associative form of `⁅H, E⁆ = 2E`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ρH_mul_ρE :
    (ρH : Module.End ℂ (StandardSl2Module ℂ n)) * ρE = ρE * ρH + (2 : ℂ) • ρE

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.ρH_mul_ρF
declarations.doc: `HF = FH - 2F` on `V(n)`, the associative form of `⁅H, F⁆ = -2F`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ρH_mul_ρF :
    (ρH : Module.End ℂ (StandardSl2Module ℂ n)) * ρF = ρF * ρH + (-2 : ℂ) • ρF

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.stdJx
declarations.statement: def stdJx : Module.End ℂ (StandardSl2Module ℂ n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.stdJy
declarations.statement: def stdJy : Module.End ℂ (StandardSl2Module ℂ n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.stdJz
declarations.doc: `Jz = H/2` on `V(n)`.
declarations.statement: def stdJz : Module.End ℂ (StandardSl2Module ℂ n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.stdJx_stdJy
declarations.statement: lemma stdJx_stdJy : ⁅stdJx n, stdJy n⁆ = Complex.I • stdJz n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.stdJy_stdJz
declarations.statement: lemma stdJy_stdJz : ⁅stdJy n, stdJz n⁆ = Complex.I • stdJx n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.stdJz_stdJx
declarations.statement: lemma stdJz_stdJx : ⁅stdJz n, stdJx n⁆ = Complex.I • stdJy n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.standard
declarations.doc:
The spin-`n/2` representation on `V(n)`: `Jz = H/2`, `Jx = (E + F)/2`,
`Jy = -i(E - F)/2`, so that `J+ = E` and `J- = F`.
declarations.statement: def standard : AngularMomentumRepresentation (StandardSl2Module ℂ n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.standard_Jp
declarations.statement: lemma standard_Jp : (standard n).Jp = ρE

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.standard_Jm
declarations.statement: lemma standard_Jm : (standard n).Jm = ρF

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.standard_Jz
declarations.statement: lemma standard_Jz : (standard n).Jz = (1 / 2 : ℂ) • ρH

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupled
declarations.doc: The coupled representation of spins `m/2` and `n/2` on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev coupled (m n : ℕ) :
    AngularMomentumRepresentation (StandardSl2Module ℂ m ⊗[ℂ] StandardSl2Module ℂ n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupled_Jz
declarations.statement: lemma coupled_Jz : (coupled m n).Jz = (1 / 2 : ℂ) • tensorH m n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupled_Jp
declarations.statement: lemma coupled_Jp : (coupled m n).Jp = tensorE m n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupled_Jm
declarations.statement: lemma coupled_Jm : (coupled m n).Jm = tensorF m n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Jz_coupled_stringVec
declarations.doc: `Jz` acts on the `l`-th vector of the `k`-th string by `J - l`, `J = (m + n - 2k)/2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jz_coupled_stringVec (l : ℕ) :
    (coupled m n).Jz (stringVec m n k l) =
      (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : ℂ) / 2 - l) • stringVec m n k l

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.Jsq_coupled_stringVec
declarations.doc: The total `J²` acts on the `k`-th string by `J(J + 1)`, `J = (m + n - 2k)/2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_coupled_stringVec (l : ℕ) :
    (coupled m n).Jsq (stringVec m n k l) =
      (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : ℂ) / 2 * (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : ℂ) / 2 + 1)) •
        stringVec m n k l

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sumEnd_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma sumEnd_smul (c : ℂ) (A : ∀ k, Module.End ℂ (CGSummand ℂ m n k)) (y : CGSum ℂ m n) :
    sumEnd (fun k => c • A k) y = c • sumEnd A y

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_Jz_coupled
declarations.doc: `cgEquiv` intertwines the total `Jz` with `Jz` of the spin-`J` summands.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgEquiv_Jz_coupled (hmn : 0 < m + n)
    (x : StandardSl2Module ℂ m ⊗[ℂ] StandardSl2Module ℂ n) :
    cgEquiv hmn ((coupled m n).Jz x) = sumEnd (fun _ => (standard _).Jz) (cgEquiv hmn x)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_Jp_coupled
declarations.doc: `cgEquiv` intertwines the total `J+` with `J+` of the spin-`J` summands.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgEquiv_Jp_coupled (hmn : 0 < m + n)
    (x : StandardSl2Module ℂ m ⊗[ℂ] StandardSl2Module ℂ n) :
    cgEquiv hmn ((coupled m n).Jp x) = sumEnd (fun _ => (standard _).Jp) (cgEquiv hmn x)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgEquiv_Jm_coupled
declarations.doc: `cgEquiv` intertwines the total `J-` with `J-` of the spin-`J` summands.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgEquiv_Jm_coupled (hmn : 0 < m + n)
    (x : StandardSl2Module ℂ m ⊗[ℂ] StandardSl2Module ℂ n) :
    cgEquiv hmn ((coupled m n).Jm x) = sumEnd (fun _ => (standard _).Jm) (cgEquiv hmn x)

modules.title: Abstract angular momentum representations
modules.doc:
Packages three endomorphisms obeying the angular momentum commutation relations and
connects them to `sl₂`.

## i. Overview

The commutation relations for three complex-linear angular momentum operators determine an
`sl₂` triple with Cartan operator `2Jz` and raising and lowering operators `Jp` and `Jm`.
This lets Mathlib’s primitive-vector theory classify finite-dimensional irreducible
representations. The square `Jx² + Jy² + Jz²` commutes with the three operators and acts as
`j(j+1)` on an irreducible representation of highest weight `2j`.

## ii. Key results

- `AngularMomentumRepresentation` records the angular momentum commutators.
- `isSl2Triple` identifies `2Jz`, `Jp`, and `Jm` with an `sl₂` triple.
- `Jsq_eq_smul` gives the Casimir eigenvalue on an irreducible representation.
- `magneticBasisVec` defines the lowering-string vectors; no basis theorem is asserted here.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Angular momentum and its `sl₂` triple
  - A.1. Spin classification

## iv. References

- Mathlib, `Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.Sl2`.

## A. Angular momentum and its `sl₂` triple

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation
declarations.doc:
Angular momentum representation. Three operators
`Jx, Jy, Jz` on a state space `V`, satisfying the `so(3)` commutation relations
`[Jx,Jy] = iJz` and cyclic permutations. (The physical requirement that they be
self-adjoint on a Hilbert space is out of scope for this algebraic model.)
declarations.statement:
structure AngularMomentumRepresentation where
  /-- The first Cartesian component of angular momentum. -/
  Jx : Module.End ℂ V
  /-- The second Cartesian component of angular momentum. -/
  Jy : Module.End ℂ V
  /-- The third Cartesian component of angular momentum. -/
  Jz : Module.End ℂ V
  comm_xy : ⁅Jx, Jy⁆ = Complex.I • Jz
  comm_yz : ⁅Jy, Jz⁆ = Complex.I • Jx
  comm_zx : ⁅Jz, Jx⁆ = Complex.I • Jy

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jp
declarations.doc: Ladder operators. `J± := Jx ± iJy`.
declarations.statement: def Jp (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) : Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jm
declarations.statement: def Jm (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) : Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.comm_z_p
declarations.doc:
Commutation relations for the ladder operators:
`[Jz, J±] = ±J±` and `[J+, J-] = 2Jz`.
declarations.statement: lemma comm_z_p (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) : ⁅ρ.Jz, ρ.Jp⁆ = ρ.Jp

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.comm_z_m
declarations.statement: lemma comm_z_m (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) : ⁅ρ.Jz, ρ.Jm⁆ = -ρ.Jm

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.comm_p_m
declarations.statement:
lemma comm_p_m (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) :
    ⁅ρ.Jp, ρ.Jm⁆ = (2 : ℂ) • ρ.Jz

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.isSl2Triple
declarations.doc:
Angular momentum generates an `sl₂`-triple, via
`h := 2 • Jz`, `e := J+`, `f := J-` (the doubling of `Jz` reconciles the physicists'
normalization `[Jz,J±]=±J±` with the `sl₂`-triple normalization `[h,e]=2e`).

The hypothesis `ρ.Jz ≠ 0` is necessary: the all-zero representation
(`Jx = Jy = Jz = 0`) satisfies every field of `AngularMomentumRepresentation`
but gives `h = 2 • Jz = 0`, which `IsSl2Triple` explicitly excludes
(`h_ne_zero`) — the trivial, spin-`0` representation does not generate an
honest copy of `sl₂` inside `End(V)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSl2Triple (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) :
    IsSl2Triple ((2 : ℂ) • ρ.Jz) ρ.Jp ρ.Jm

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.IsIrreducible
declarations.doc:
Irreducibility of an angular momentum representation: no proper subspace is
invariant under `Jx`, `Jy`, and `Jz` simultaneously.
declarations.statement: def IsIrreducible (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) : Prop

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jx_mem_sl2
declarations.doc:
Irreducibility transfers along the bridge:
`ρ.IsIrreducible` agrees with irreducibility of the induced module for the `sl₂`-subalgebra
generated by `(2Jz, J+, J-)` (via the automatic `LieSubalgebra.lieRingModule`/`lieModule`
instances restricting the tautological `Module.End ℂ V`-action on `V`).
declarations.statement:
lemma Jx_mem_sl2 (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) :
    ρ.Jx ∈ (ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jy_mem_sl2
declarations.statement:
lemma Jy_mem_sl2 (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) :
    ρ.Jy ∈ (ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jz_mem_sl2
declarations.statement:
lemma Jz_mem_sl2 (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) :
    ρ.Jz ∈ (ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jp_mem_of_invariant
declarations.statement:
lemma Jp_mem_of_invariant (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (W : Submodule ℂ V) (hx : ∀ v ∈ W, ρ.Jx v ∈ W)
    (hy : ∀ v ∈ W, ρ.Jy v ∈ W) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ W) : ρ.Jp v ∈ W

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jm_mem_of_invariant
declarations.statement:
lemma Jm_mem_of_invariant (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (W : Submodule ℂ V) (hx : ∀ v ∈ W, ρ.Jx v ∈ W)
    (hy : ∀ v ∈ W, ρ.Jy v ∈ W) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ W) : ρ.Jm v ∈ W

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.sl2_invariant_of_angular_invariant
declarations.statement:
lemma sl2_invariant_of_angular_invariant (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) (W : Submodule ℂ V)
    (hx : ∀ v ∈ W, ρ.Jx v ∈ W) (hy : ∀ v ∈ W, ρ.Jy v ∈ W)
    (hzW : ∀ v ∈ W, ρ.Jz v ∈ W) {x : ↥((ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ)}
    {v : V} (hv : v ∈ W) : ⁅x, v⁆ ∈ W

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.nontrivial_of_Jz_ne_zero
declarations.doc: A nonzero `Jz` forces the representation space to be nontrivial.
declarations.statement:
lemma nontrivial_of_Jz_ne_zero (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) :
    Nontrivial V

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.lieSubmodule_stable
declarations.doc: Lie submodules are stable under every operator in the generated subalgebra.

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.angular_irreducible_implies_sl2
declarations.statement:
lemma angular_irreducible_implies_sl2 (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) (hirr : ρ.IsIrreducible) :
    LieModule.IsIrreducible ℂ ↥((ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ) V

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.sl2_irreducible_implies_angular
declarations.statement:
lemma sl2_irreducible_implies_angular (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0)
    (hirr : LieModule.IsIrreducible ℂ ↥((ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ) V) :
    ρ.IsIrreducible

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.isIrreducible_iff
declarations.doc:
Invariance under `Jx`, `Jy`, `Jz` is equivalent to irreducibility for the generated
`sl₂` Lie subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIrreducible_iff (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) :
    ρ.IsIrreducible ↔ LieModule.IsIrreducible ℂ (↥((ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ)) V

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.spin_classification
declarations.doc:
A finite-dimensional irreducible angular momentum representation is isomorphic to a
standard `sl₂` module for the subalgebra generated by `(2Jz, Jp, Jm)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma spin_classification [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) (hirr : ρ.IsIrreducible) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, letI := standardSl2ModuleLieRingModule (K := ℂ) (n := n) (ρ.isSl2Triple hz)
      Nonempty (V ≃ₗ⁅ℂ, ↥((ρ.isSl2Triple hz).toLieSubalgebra ℂ)⁆ StandardSl2Module ℂ n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jp_mul_Jm
declarations.doc:
`J+J- = Jx²+Jy²+Jz`: the standard ladder-operator identity, a purely algebraic
consequence of the commutation relations (no representation theory needed). Used to
reduce `Jsq_eq_smul` to a statement about `Jp * Jm`, via
`J² = Jp*Jm + Jz*Jz - Jz` (equivalently `Jm*Jp + Jz*Jz + Jz`).
declarations.statement:
lemma Jp_mul_Jm (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) :
    ρ.Jp * ρ.Jm = ρ.Jx * ρ.Jx + ρ.Jy * ρ.Jy + ρ.Jz

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_eq_Jp_mul_Jm
declarations.doc:
`J² = J+J- + Jz² - Jz`: a purely algebraic consequence of the commutation
relations (no representation theory needed), used to reduce `Jsq_eq_smul` to a
statement about the ladder operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_eq_Jp_mul_Jm (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) :
    ρ.Jx * ρ.Jx + ρ.Jy * ρ.Jy + ρ.Jz * ρ.Jz =
      ρ.Jp * ρ.Jm + ρ.Jz * ρ.Jz - ρ.Jz

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.leibniz_end
declarations.doc:
Product Leibniz rule for the associative-ring bracket on `Module.End ℂ V`:
`⁅a*x, z⁆ = a*⁅x,z⁆ + ⁅a,z⁆*x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma leibniz_end (a x z : Module.End ℂ V) :
    (⁅a * x, z⁆ : Module.End ℂ V) = a * ⁅x, z⁆ + ⁅a, z⁆ * x

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.mul_eq_of_lie_eq
declarations.doc: Unfolds the associative-ring bracket relation `⁅a, b⁆ = c` into `a * b = b * a + c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_eq_of_lie_eq {a b c : Module.End ℂ V} (h : (⁅a, b⁆ : Module.End ℂ V) = c) :
    a * b = b * a + c

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_comm_p
declarations.doc:
`J²` commutes with `J+`: a step towards showing `J²` is central, hence (on an
irreducible module) acts as a scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_comm_p (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) :
    (⁅ρ.Jx * ρ.Jx + ρ.Jy * ρ.Jy + ρ.Jz * ρ.Jz, ρ.Jp⁆ : Module.End ℂ V) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_comm_m
declarations.doc:
`J²` commutes with `J-`: a step towards showing `J²` is central, hence (on an
irreducible module) acts as a scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_comm_m (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) :
    (⁅ρ.Jx * ρ.Jx + ρ.Jy * ρ.Jy + ρ.Jz * ρ.Jz, ρ.Jm⁆ : Module.End ℂ V) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_comm_z
declarations.doc:
`J²` commutes with `Jz`: derived from `Jsq_comm_p`/`Jsq_comm_m` via the Jacobi
identity, since `2•Jz = ⁅Jp,Jm⁆`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_comm_z (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) :
    (⁅ρ.Jx * ρ.Jx + ρ.Jy * ρ.Jy + ρ.Jz * ρ.Jz, ρ.Jz⁆ : Module.End ℂ V) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq
declarations.doc: The quadratic angular momentum operator `Jx² + Jy² + Jz²`.
declarations.statement: def Jsq (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) : Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.JpJm_on_primitive
declarations.doc: On a primitive vector of weight `n`, `Jp Jm` acts by `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma JpJm_on_primitive (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0)
    {n : ℕ} {v : V} (P : (ρ.isSl2Triple hz).HasPrimitiveVectorWith v (n : ℂ)) :
    ρ.Jp (ρ.Jm v) = (n : ℂ) • v

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jz_on_primitive
declarations.doc: The Cartan operator acts by half the highest weight on a primitive vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jz_on_primitive (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0)
    {n : ℕ} {v : V} (P : (ρ.isSl2Triple hz).HasPrimitiveVectorWith v (n : ℂ)) :
    ρ.Jz v = ((n : ℂ) / 2) • v

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_on_primitive
declarations.doc: The quadratic operator has the expected eigenvalue on a primitive vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_on_primitive (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0)
    {n : ℕ} {v : V} (P : (ρ.isSl2Triple hz).HasPrimitiveVectorWith v (n : ℂ)) :
    ρ.Jsq v = ((n : ℂ) / 2 * ((n : ℂ) / 2 + 1)) • v

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.ker_scalar_stable
declarations.doc: An eigenspace of an endomorphism is stable under commuting endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_scalar_stable (C A : Module.End ℂ V) (c : ℂ)
    (hCA : (⁅C, A⁆ : Module.End ℂ V) = 0)
    {v : V} (hv : v ∈ LinearMap.ker (C - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V))) :
    A v ∈ LinearMap.ker (C - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jx_apply_eq
declarations.doc: `Jx` is half the sum of the ladder operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jx_apply_eq (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (v : V) :
    ρ.Jx v = ((1 : ℂ) / 2) • (ρ.Jp v + ρ.Jm v)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jy_apply_eq
declarations.doc: `Jy` is `-i/2` times the difference of the ladder operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jy_apply_eq (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (v : V) :
    ρ.Jy v = (-(Complex.I / 2)) • (ρ.Jp v - ρ.Jm v)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_ker_stable_x
declarations.doc: The `J²` eigenspace is stable under `Jx`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_ker_stable_x (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (c : ℂ)
    {v : V} (hv : v ∈ LinearMap.ker (ρ.Jsq - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V))) :
    ρ.Jx v ∈ LinearMap.ker (ρ.Jsq - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_ker_stable_y
declarations.doc: The `J²` eigenspace is stable under `Jy`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_ker_stable_y (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (c : ℂ)
    {v : V} (hv : v ∈ LinearMap.ker (ρ.Jsq - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V))) :
    ρ.Jy v ∈ LinearMap.ker (ρ.Jsq - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_ker_eq_top
declarations.doc: A nonzero vector in a `J²` eigenspace forces that eigenspace to be everything.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_ker_eq_top (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hirr : ρ.IsIrreducible) (c : ℂ) {v : V} (hv : v ≠ 0)
    (hmem : v ∈ LinearMap.ker (ρ.Jsq - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V))) :
    LinearMap.ker (ρ.Jsq - c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V)) = ⊤

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_eq_scalar_of_eigenvector
declarations.doc: A nonzero `J²` eigenvector forces `J²` to be that scalar on an irreducible module.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_eq_scalar_of_eigenvector (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hirr : ρ.IsIrreducible) (c : ℂ) {v : V} (hv : v ≠ 0)
    (hCv : ρ.Jsq v = c • v) : ρ.Jsq = c • (1 : Module.End ℂ V)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_eq_zero_of_Jz_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `Jz = 0`, the commutation relations force all three angular momentum operators
to vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_eq_zero_of_Jz_eq_zero (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hz : ρ.Jz = 0) : ρ.Jsq = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.Jsq_eq_smul
declarations.doc:
On an irreducible finite-dimensional representation, `J²` acts by `j(j+1)` for
some `j = n/2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Jsq_eq_smul [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V)
    (hirr : ρ.IsIrreducible) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ρ.Jsq = ((n : ℂ) / 2 * ((n : ℂ) / 2 + 1)) • (1 : Module.End ℂ V)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.AngularMomentumRepresentation.magneticBasisVec
declarations.doc:
Magnetic-weight ladder vectors: given a primitive vector
`v₀` of weight `n` for the triple `(2Jz, J+, J-)`, this defines `(J-)ᵏ v₀` for
`k = 0,…,n`. A basis theorem and reindexing by `m = n/2 - k` remain to be added.
declarations.statement:
def magneticBasisVec (ρ : AngularMomentumRepresentation V) (hz : ρ.Jz ≠ 0) {n : ℕ} {v₀ : V}
    (_ : (ρ.isSl2Triple hz).HasPrimitiveVectorWith v₀ (n : ℂ)) (k : Fin (n + 1)) : V

modules.title: A two-qubit circuit for the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients of two spins ½
modules.doc:
The change of basis from the product basis to the coupled basis of two spins `1/2` as a
two-qubit circuit.

## i. Overview

A spin `1/2` is a qubit with `|↑⟩ = |0⟩` and `|↓⟩ = |1⟩`. The product basis of two spins is
indexed by `Qubit × Qubit`, in the order `|00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, |11⟩ = |↑↑⟩, |↑↓⟩, |↓↑⟩, |↓↓⟩`; the
first qubit is the first spin. The coupled basis is indexed by `Qubit × Qubit` as well, the
columns `(0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1)` being the triplet states `|1, 1⟩, |1, 0⟩, |1, -1⟩` and the
singlet `|0, 0⟩`. The matrix `cgMatrix` of the change of basis has the Clebsch–Gordan
coefficients `cgCoefficient 1 1 k l a b` of `ClebschGordanCoefficients` as entries, with
Condon–Shortley phases.

It is the matrix of the circuit which first applies a Hadamard gate to the first qubit
controlled by the second (`CH21`), then the CNOT gate with the first qubit as control:
`CNOT * CH21 = cgMatrix` (`cnot_mul_CH21`). In particular `cgMatrix` is unitary
(`cgMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup`).

## ii. Key results

- `cgMatrix`: the Clebsch–Gordan matrix of two spins `1/2`.
- `CH21`: the controlled Hadamard gate with the second qubit as control.
- `cnot_mul_CH21`: the circuit `CNOT * CH21` is the Clebsch–Gordan matrix.
- `cgMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup`: the Clebsch–Gordan matrix is unitary.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Clebsch–Gordan matrix and the circuit

## iv. References

- The Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and their phase convention are those of
  `ClebschGordanCoefficients`; the gates are those of `QuantumInfo.States.Pure.Qubit`.

## A. The Clebsch–Gordan matrix and the circuit

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgK
declarations.doc:
The label `k` of the coupled state in column `q`: `0` for the triplet, `1` for the singlet
`q = (1, 1)`.
declarations.statement: def cgK (q : Qubit × Qubit) : ℕ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgL
declarations.doc:
The label `l = J - M` of the coupled state in column `q`: the columns `(0,0), (0,1), (1,0)`
are the triplet states with `M = 1, 0, -1`, the column `(1,1)` the singlet.
declarations.statement: def cgL (q : Qubit × Qubit) : ℕ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgMatrix
declarations.doc:
The Clebsch–Gordan matrix of two spins `1/2`: the entry in row `(a, b)` and column `q` is
`⟨½ m₁ ½ m₂ | J M⟩` with `m₁ = ½ - a`, `m₂ = ½ - b` and `J, M` given by `cgK q`, `cgL q`.
declarations.statement: def cgMatrix : Matrix (Qubit × Qubit) (Qubit × Qubit) ℂ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.CH21
declarations.doc: The Hadamard gate on the first qubit controlled by the second qubit.
declarations.statement: def CH21 : Matrix (Qubit × Qubit) (Qubit × Qubit) ℂ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cnot_mul_CH21
declarations.doc: The circuit `CH21` followed by `CNOT` is the Clebsch–Gordan matrix of two spins `1/2`.
declarations.statement: lemma cnot_mul_CH21 : CNOT.val * CH21 = cgMatrix

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.CH21_mem_unitaryGroup
declarations.doc: `CH21` is unitary, as a reindexing of the unitary `C[H]`.
declarations.statement: lemma CH21_mem_unitaryGroup : CH21 ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup (Qubit × Qubit) ℂ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup
declarations.doc: The Clebsch–Gordan matrix of two spins `1/2` is unitary.
declarations.statement: lemma cgMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup : cgMatrix ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup (Qubit × Qubit) ℂ

modules.title: Clebsch–Gordan coefficients
modules.doc:
The orthonormal coupled basis `|J, M⟩` of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` over `ℝ` and the Clebsch–Gordan
coefficients `⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩` in the standard normalisation and phase convention.

## i. Overview

The contravariant forms on `V(m)` and `V(n)` combine to a symmetric bilinear form on
`V(m) ⊗ V(n)` for which the diagonal raising and lowering operators are adjoint. For the
lowering strings `f^l w_k` of the highest-weight vectors `w_k` this gives

`⟨f^a w_k, f^b w_{k'}⟩ = δ_{kk'} δ_{ab} · a! N!/(N - a)! · ⟨w_k, w_k⟩`,  `N = m + n - 2k`,

and `⟨w_k, w_k⟩ > 0`. Normalising gives the orthonormal coupled basis
`|J, M⟩ = coupledVec m n k l` with `J = (m + n)/2 - k`, `M = J - l`, on which `J₊, J₋`
act by the textbook formulas. The Clebsch–Gordan coefficient is the inner product

`⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ = cgCoefficient m n k l a b = ⟨u_a ⊗ u_b, |J, M⟩⟩`

with `j₁ = m/2`, `m₁ = j₁ - a`, `j₂ = n/2`, `m₂ = j₂ - b`. This file proves:

- the coupled states are orthonormal and satisfy the ladder relations of `|J, M⟩`;
- `⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ = 0` unless `m₁ + m₂ = M`;
- the Condon–Shortley phase convention `⟨j₁ j₁ j₂ (J - j₁) | J J⟩ > 0`;
- every coupled state is `Σ ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ |j₁ m₁⟩ ⊗ |j₂ m₂⟩`, and the orthogonality
  relation `Σ_{m₁ m₂} ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J' M'⟩ = δ_{JJ'} δ_{MM'}`;
- the values `⟨j₁ j₁ j₂ j₂ | j₁+j₂, j₁+j₂⟩ = 1`, and for two spins `1/2` the singlet
  `⟨½ ½ ½ -½ | 0 0⟩ = 1/√2`, `⟨½ -½ ½ ½ | 0 0⟩ = -1/√2` and the triplet
  `⟨½ ½ ½ -½ | 1 0⟩ = ⟨½ -½ ½ ½ | 1 0⟩ = 1/√2`, `⟨½ -½ ½ -½ | 1 -1⟩ = 1`.

These properties determine the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients uniquely, so they agree with the
tabulated values. A closed formula (Racah's formula) is not proved here.

## ii. Key results

- `tensorForm`, `tensorForm_tensorF` (contravariance) and `tensorForm_stringVec`.
- `hwNormSq_pos`, `coupledVec`, `tensorForm_coupledVec` (orthonormality),
  `tensorF_coupledVec`, `tensorE_coupledVec_succ` (ladder relations).
- `cgCoefficient`, `cgCoefficient_eq_zero_of_ne`, `cgCoefficient_top_pos`,
  `coupledVec_eq_sum`, `sum_cgCoefficient_mul`.
- `cgCoefficient_stretched`, `cgCoefficient_singlet_up`, `cgCoefficient_singlet_down`,
  `cgCoefficient_triplet_zero_up`, `cgCoefficient_triplet_zero_down`,
  `cgCoefficient_triplet_minus`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The form on the tensor product
- B. Inner products of the lowering strings
- C. The orthonormal coupled basis
- D. Clebsch–Gordan coefficients
  - D.1. Definition, weight rule and phase
  - D.2. Expansion and orthogonality
  - D.3. Values

## iv. References

- J. J. Sakurai and J. Napolitano, *Modern Quantum Mechanics*, 3rd ed., Cambridge University
  Press (2020), section 3.8.

## A. The form on the tensor product

sections.text: ## B. Inner products of the lowering strings

## D. Clebsch–Gordan coefficients

### D.1. Definition, weight rule and phase

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm
declarations.doc: The contravariant form on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`: `⟨x ⊗ y, x' ⊗ y'⟩ = ⟨x, x'⟩ ⟨y, y'⟩`.
declarations.statement: def tensorForm : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ (StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_tmul (x x' : StandardSl2Module ℝ m) (y y' : StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    tensorForm m n (x ⊗ₜ y) (x' ⊗ₜ y') = invForm ℝ m x x' * invForm ℝ n y y'

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorBilin_ext
declarations.doc: Two bilinear forms on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` agree if they agree on pure tensors.

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_ρE_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma invForm_ρE_apply (x y : StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    invForm ℝ n (ρE x) y = invForm ℝ n x (ρF y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_ρH_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma invForm_ρH_apply (x y : StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    invForm ℝ n (ρH x) y = invForm ℝ n x (ρH y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_comm
declarations.doc: The form on the tensor product is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_comm (x y : StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    tensorForm m n x y = tensorForm m n y x

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_tensorE
declarations.doc: The diagonal raising and lowering operators are adjoint: `⟨E x, y⟩ = ⟨x, F y⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_tensorE (x y : StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    tensorForm m n (tensorE m n x) y = tensorForm m n x (tensorF m n y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_tensorF
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_tensorF (x y : StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    tensorForm m n (tensorF m n x) y = tensorForm m n x (tensorE m n y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_tensorH
declarations.doc: The diagonal weight operator is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_tensorH (x y : StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    tensorForm m n (tensorH m n x) y = tensorForm m n x (tensorH m n y)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_hwVec_of_ne
declarations.doc: Highest-weight vectors of different weight are orthogonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_hwVec_of_ne {k k' : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ k') :
    tensorForm m n (hwVec m n k) (hwVec m n k') = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.stringVec_zero'
declarations.statement: lemma stringVec_zero' (k : ℕ) : stringVec (K := ℝ) m n k 0 = hwVec m n k

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_stringVec
declarations.doc:
The inner products of the lowering strings:
`⟨f^a w_k, f^b w_{k'}⟩ = δ_{kk'} δ_{ab} · normSq (m + n - 2k) a · ⟨w_k, w_k⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_stringVec (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k k' : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (hk'm : k' ≤ m) (hk'n : k' ≤ n) (a b : ℕ) :
    tensorForm m n (stringVec m n k a) (stringVec m n k' b) =
      if k = k' ∧ a = b then
        (normSq (m + n - 2 * k) a : ℝ) * tensorForm m n (hwVec m n k) (hwVec m n k)
      else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormSq
declarations.doc: The squared norm `⟨w_k, w_k⟩` of the highest-weight vector `w_k`.
declarations.statement: def hwNormSq (k : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormSq_eq
declarations.doc: `⟨w_k, w_k⟩ = Σ_a cgCoeff(a)² · normSq m a · normSq n (k - a)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hwNormSq_eq {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    hwNormSq m n k = ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
      cgCoeff (K := ℝ) m n k a ^ 2 * (normSq m a : ℝ) * (normSq n (k - a) : ℝ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoeff_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoeff_zero (k : ℕ) :
    cgCoeff (K := ℝ) m n k 0 = ((n - k).factorial * m.factorial : ℕ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormSq_pos
declarations.statement: lemma hwNormSq_pos {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) : 0 < hwNormSq m n k

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupledVec
declarations.doc: The normalised coupled state `|J, M⟩` with `J = (m + n)/2 - k`, `M = J - l`.
declarations.statement: def coupledVec (k l : ℕ) : StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_coupledVec
declarations.doc: The coupled states are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_coupledVec (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k k' l l' : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (hk'm : k' ≤ m) (hk'n : k' ≤ n) (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) :
    tensorForm m n (coupledVec m n k l) (coupledVec m n k' l') =
      if k = k' ∧ l = l' then 1 else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sqrt_coupled_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma sqrt_coupled_succ {k l : ℕ} :
    Real.sqrt ((normSq (m + n - 2 * k) (l + 1) : ℝ) * hwNormSq m n k) =
      Real.sqrt ((normSq (m + n - 2 * k) l : ℝ) * hwNormSq m n k) *
        Real.sqrt (((l : ℝ) + 1) * (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : ℝ) - l))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF_coupledVec
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorF_coupledVec {k l : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (hl : l < m + n - 2 * k) :
    tensorF m n (coupledVec m n k l) =
      Real.sqrt (((l : ℝ) + 1) * (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : ℝ) - l)) • coupledVec m n k (l + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorE_coupledVec_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorE_coupledVec_succ (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k l : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (hl : l < m + n - 2 * k) :
    tensorE m n (coupledVec m n k (l + 1)) =
      Real.sqrt (((l : ℝ) + 1) * (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : ℝ) - l)) • coupledVec m n k l

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient
declarations.doc:
The Clebsch–Gordan coefficient `⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ = ⟨u_a ⊗ u_b, |J, M⟩⟩` with `j₁ = m/2`,
`m₁ = j₁ - a`, `j₂ = n/2`, `m₂ = j₂ - b`, `J = (m + n)/2 - k` and `M = J - l`.
declarations.statement: def cgCoefficient (k l a b : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH_normVec_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorH_normVec_tmul (a b : ℕ) :
    tensorH m n (normVec m a ⊗ₜ normVec n b) =
      (((m : ℝ) - 2 * a) + ((n : ℝ) - 2 * b)) • (normVec m a ⊗ₜ normVec n b)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorH_coupledVec
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorH_coupledVec (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (l : ℕ) :
    tensorH m n (coupledVec m n k l) =
      (((m + n - 2 * k : ℕ) : ℝ) - 2 * l) • coupledVec m n k l

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_eq_zero_of_ne
declarations.doc: **Weight rule.** `⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ = 0` unless `m₁ + m₂ = M`, i.e. `a + b = k + l`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_eq_zero_of_ne (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k l a b : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (h : a + b ≠ k + l) : cgCoefficient m n k l a b = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_normVec_vNat
declarations.statement:
lemma invForm_normVec_vNat {a : ℕ} (ha : a ≤ n) (c : ℕ) :
    invForm ℝ n (normVec n a) (vNat n c) = if a = c then Real.sqrt (normSq n a) else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_normVec_hwVec
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_normVec_hwVec {k a : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (ha : a ≤ k) :
    tensorForm m n (normVec m a ⊗ₜ normVec n (k - a)) (hwVec m n k) =
      cgCoeff m n k a * Real.sqrt (normSq m a) * Real.sqrt (normSq n (k - a))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_top
declarations.doc:
The coefficients of the top state `|J, J⟩`:
`⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J J⟩ = cgCoeff(a) · √(normSq m a) · √(normSq n (k - a)) / √⟨w_k, w_k⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_top {k a : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (ha : a ≤ k) :
    cgCoefficient m n k 0 a (k - a) =
      cgCoeff m n k a * Real.sqrt (normSq m a) * Real.sqrt (normSq n (k - a)) /
        Real.sqrt (hwNormSq m n k)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_top_pos
declarations.doc: **Condon–Shortley phase convention.** `⟨j₁ j₁ j₂ (J - j₁) | J J⟩ > 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_top_pos {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    0 < cgCoefficient m n k 0 0 k

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.eq_sum_normVec
declarations.doc: Every vector of `V(n)` is `Σ_a ⟨u_a, x⟩ u_a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_normVec (x : StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    x = ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), invForm ℝ n (normVec n a) x • normVec n a

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.eq_sum_normVec_tmul
declarations.doc: Every vector of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` is `Σ_{a b} ⟨u_a ⊗ u_b, x⟩ u_a ⊗ u_b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_normVec_tmul (x : StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    x = ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      tensorForm m n (normVec m a ⊗ₜ normVec n b) x • (normVec m a ⊗ₜ normVec n b)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupledVec_eq_sum
declarations.doc: `|J, M⟩ = Σ_{m₁ m₂} ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ |j₁ m₁⟩ ⊗ |j₂ m₂⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coupledVec_eq_sum (k l : ℕ) :
    coupledVec m n k l = ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      cgCoefficient m n k l a b • (normVec m a ⊗ₜ normVec n b)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sum_cgCoefficient_mul
declarations.doc:
**Orthogonality relation.**
`Σ_{m₁ m₂} ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J' M'⟩ = δ_{JJ'} δ_{MM'}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_cgCoefficient_mul (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k k' l l' : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (hk'm : k' ≤ m) (hk'n : k' ≤ n) (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) :
    ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
      cgCoefficient m n k l a b * cgCoefficient m n k' l' a b =
        if k = k' ∧ l = l' then 1 else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormSq_zero
declarations.statement: lemma hwNormSq_zero : hwNormSq m n 0 = ((n.factorial * m.factorial : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ 2

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_stretched
declarations.doc: `⟨j₁ j₁ j₂ j₂ | j₁+j₂, j₁+j₂⟩ = 1`.
declarations.statement: lemma cgCoefficient_stretched : cgCoefficient m n 0 0 0 0 = 1

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormSq_one_one
declarations.statement: lemma hwNormSq_one_one : hwNormSq 1 1 1 = 2

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_singlet_up
declarations.doc: Singlet: `⟨½ ½ ½ -½ | 0 0⟩ = 1/√2`.
declarations.statement: lemma cgCoefficient_singlet_up : cgCoefficient 1 1 1 0 0 1 = 1 / Real.sqrt 2

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_singlet_down
declarations.doc: Singlet: `⟨½ -½ ½ ½ | 0 0⟩ = -1/√2`.
declarations.statement: lemma cgCoefficient_singlet_down : cgCoefficient 1 1 1 0 1 0 = -1 / Real.sqrt 2

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupledVec_one_one_zero_one
declarations.statement:
lemma coupledVec_one_one_zero_one :
    coupledVec 1 1 0 1 = (1 / Real.sqrt 2) • tensorF 1 1 (coupledVec 1 1 0 0)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_normVec_one_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ρE_normVec_one_zero : (ρE : Module.End ℝ (StandardSl2Module ℝ 1)) (normVec 1 0) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_normVec_one_one
declarations.statement:
lemma ρE_normVec_one_one :
    (ρE : Module.End ℝ (StandardSl2Module ℝ 1)) (normVec 1 1) = normVec 1 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_triplet_zero_up
declarations.doc: Triplet: `⟨½ ½ ½ -½ | 1 0⟩ = 1/√2`.
declarations.statement: lemma cgCoefficient_triplet_zero_up : cgCoefficient 1 1 0 1 0 1 = 1 / Real.sqrt 2

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_triplet_zero_down
declarations.doc: Triplet: `⟨½ -½ ½ ½ | 1 0⟩ = 1/√2`.
declarations.statement: lemma cgCoefficient_triplet_zero_down : cgCoefficient 1 1 0 1 1 0 = 1 / Real.sqrt 2

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.coupledVec_one_one_zero_two
declarations.statement:
lemma coupledVec_one_one_zero_two :
    coupledVec 1 1 0 2 = (1 / Real.sqrt 2) • tensorF 1 1 (coupledVec 1 1 0 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_triplet_minus
declarations.doc: Triplet: `⟨½ -½ ½ -½ | 1 -1⟩ = 1`.
declarations.statement: lemma cgCoefficient_triplet_minus : cgCoefficient 1 1 0 2 1 1 = 1

modules.title: Closed formulas for the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients
modules.doc:
The second orthogonality relation, an explicit single-sum formula and Racah's formula for
`⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩`.

## i. Overview

The coupled states `|J, M⟩` form an orthonormal basis of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)`, so every vector is
`Σ_{J M} ⟨J M | x⟩ |J M⟩`. Applied to product states this gives the second orthogonality relation
`Σ_{J M} ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ ⟨j₁ m₁' j₂ m₂' | J M⟩ = δ_{m₁ m₁'} δ_{m₂ m₂'}`.

For the closed formula, two computations are combined.

- The squared norm of the highest-weight vector `w_k` has the closed form
  `⟨w_k, w_k⟩ = k! m! n! (m - k)! (n - k)! (m + n - k + 1)! / (m + n - 2k + 1)!`.
  It reduces to the factorial identity
  `Σ_a C(k, a) (p + a)! (k + s - a)! · (p + s + 1)! = (p + k + s + 1)! p! s!`, proved by induction
  on `k` with Pascal's rule.
- The lowering operator on `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` is `f ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ f` with commuting summands, so the
  binomial theorem gives `f^l (v_a ⊗ v_b) = Σ_i C(l, i) v_{a+i} ⊗ v_{b+l-i}`.

Together with the coefficients of `w_k` from `TensorHighestWeight` this yields, with
`J = (m + n)/2 - k`, `M = J - l`, `m₁ = m/2 - α`, `m₂ = n/2 - β` and `α + β = k + l`, a formula
`⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ = S · √(…)` with the single alternating sum
`S = Σ_a (-1)^a C(k, a) C(l, α - a) (n - k + a)! (m - a)!`.

Racah's formula has a different alternating sum. After dividing out factorials both sums become
binomial sums,
`L(k, α, s) = Σ_a (-1)^a C(k, a) C(r + k - a, α - a) C(p + a, s + a)` and
`R(k, α, s) = Σ_z (-1)^z C(k, z) C(r, α - z) C(p, s + z)`,
with lower indices in `ℤ` (`C(n, j) = 0` for `j < 0`). Pascal's rule shows that both satisfy
`X(k + 1, α, s) = X(k, α, s) - X(k, α - 1, s + 1)`, and they agree for `k = 0`, so `L = R`.
This proves Racah's formula.

For `n = 1`, coupling a spin `j₁ = m/2` with a spin `½`, the single sum has at most two terms and
the closed formula gives the four coefficients in square-root form, with `J = j₁ ± ½`.

## ii. Key results

- `eq_sum_coupledVec` and `sum_cgCoefficient_mul_cgCoefficient`: completeness of the coupled basis
  and the second orthogonality relation.
- `sum_choose_mul_factorial` and `hwNormSq_closed`: the closed norm of `w_k`.
- `tensorF_pow_tmul_vNat`: the explicit lowering.
- `cgCoefficient_eq_cgSum` and `cgCoefficient_closed`: the closed single-sum formula.
- `racahL_eq_racahR` and `cgCoefficient_racah`: Racah's formula.
- `cgCoefficient_add_half_up`, `cgCoefficient_add_half_down`, `cgCoefficient_sub_half_up`,
  `cgCoefficient_sub_half_down`: the coefficients for coupling with a spin `½`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Completeness and the second orthogonality relation
- B. The norm of the highest-weight vectors
  - B.1. A factorial identity
  - B.2. The closed norm
- C. The lowering strings in the product basis
- D. The closed formula
- E. Racah's formula
  - E.1. Binomial coefficients with an integer lower index
  - E.2. Two binomial sums with the same recursion
  - E.3. Racah's formula
- F. Coupling with a spin ½

## iv. References

- G. Racah, *Theory of complex spectra. II*, Phys. Rev. 62, 438 (1942).
- J. J. Sakurai and J. Napolitano, *Modern Quantum Mechanics*, 3rd ed., Cambridge University
  Press (2020), section 3.8.
- D. A. Varshalovich, A. N. Moskalev, V. K. Khersonskii, *Quantum Theory of Angular Momentum:
  Irreducible Tensors, Spherical Harmonics, Vector Coupling Coefficients, 3nj Symbols*, World
  Scientific (1988), Table 8.1, p. 271.

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_coupledVec_stringVec
declarations.doc: `⟨|J, M⟩, f^{l'} w_{k'}⟩ = δ_{kk'} δ_{ll'} √(normSq N l · ⟨w_k, w_k⟩)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_coupledVec_stringVec (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k k' l l' : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m)
    (hkn : k ≤ n) (hk'm : k' ≤ m) (hk'n : k' ≤ n) (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) :
    tensorForm m n (coupledVec m n k l) (stringVec m n k' l') =
      if k = k' ∧ l = l' then
        Real.sqrt ((normSq (m + n - 2 * k) l : ℝ) * hwNormSq m n k)
      else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.eq_sum_coupledVec
declarations.doc: **Completeness.** Every vector of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` is `Σ_{J M} ⟨|J, M⟩, x⟩ |J, M⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_coupledVec (hmn : 0 < m + n) (x : StandardSl2Module ℝ m ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ n) :
    x = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (min m n + 1), ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (m + n - 2 * k + 1),
      tensorForm m n (coupledVec m n k l) x • coupledVec m n k l

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sum_cgCoefficient_mul_cgCoefficient
declarations.doc:
**Second orthogonality relation.**
`Σ_{J M} ⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ ⟨j₁ m₁' j₂ m₂' | J M⟩ = δ_{m₁ m₁'} δ_{m₂ m₂'}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_cgCoefficient_mul_cgCoefficient (hmn : 0 < m + n) {a b a' b' : ℕ} (ha : a ≤ m)
    (hb : b ≤ n) (ha' : a' ≤ m) (hb' : b' ≤ n) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (min m n + 1), ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (m + n - 2 * k + 1),
      cgCoefficient m n k l a b * cgCoefficient m n k l a' b' =
        if a = a' ∧ b = b' then 1 else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.factorialSum
declarations.statement: def factorialSum (k p s : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.factorialSum_succ
declarations.doc: Pascal's rule for `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma factorialSum_succ (k p s : ℕ) :
    factorialSum (k + 1) p s = factorialSum k p (s + 1) + factorialSum k (p + 1) s

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.factorialSum_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma factorialSum_mul (k p s : ℕ) :
    factorialSum k p s * (p + s + 1).factorial =
      (p + k + s + 1).factorial * p.factorial * s.factorial

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sum_choose_mul_factorial
declarations.doc:
The factorial identity in the form used for `⟨w_k, w_k⟩`:
`Σ_a C(k, a) (p + a)! (s + k - a)! · (p + s + 1)! = (p + k + s + 1)! p! s!`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_choose_mul_factorial (k p s : ℕ) :
    (∑ a ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), k.choose a * ((p + a).factorial * (s + (k - a)).factorial)) *
      (p + s + 1).factorial = (p + k + s + 1).factorial * p.factorial * s.factorial

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormNum
declarations.doc: The numerator `k! m! n! (m + n - k + 1)! (n - k)! (m - k)!` of `⟨w_k, w_k⟩`.
declarations.statement: def hwNormNum (m n k : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoeff_sq_mul_normSq
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoeff_sq_mul_normSq {k a : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (ha : a ≤ k) :
    cgCoeff (K := ℝ) m n k a ^ 2 * (normSq m a : ℝ) * (normSq n (k - a) : ℝ) =
      ((k.choose a * ((n - k + a).factorial * (m - a).factorial) *
        (k.factorial * m.factorial * n.factorial) : ℕ) : ℝ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormSq_mul_factorial
declarations.statement:
lemma hwNormSq_mul_factorial {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    hwNormSq m n k * ((m + n - 2 * k + 1).factorial : ℝ) = hwNormNum m n k

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.hwNormSq_closed
declarations.doc:
**The closed norm.**
`⟨w_k, w_k⟩ = k! m! n! (m + n - k + 1)! (n - k)! (m - k)! / (m + n - 2k + 1)!`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hwNormSq_closed {k : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
    hwNormSq m n k = hwNormNum m n k / ((m + n - 2 * k + 1).factorial : ℝ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρF_pow_vNat
declarations.statement:
lemma ρF_pow_vNat (a l : ℕ) :
    ((ρF : Module.End ℝ (StandardSl2Module ℝ n)) ^ l) (vNat n a) = vNat n (a + l)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorF_pow_tmul_vNat
declarations.doc:
The binomial theorem for the lowering operator:
`f^l (v_a ⊗ v_b) = Σ_i C(l, i) v_{a+i} ⊗ v_{b+l-i}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorF_pow_tmul_vNat (a b l : ℕ) :
    (tensorF (K := ℝ) m n ^ l) (vNat m a ⊗ₜ vNat n b) =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (l + 1), (l.choose i : ℝ) • (vNat m (a + i) ⊗ₜ vNat n (b + (l - i)))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgSum
declarations.doc: The alternating sum `Σ_{a ≤ min(k, α)} (-1)^a C(k, a) (n - k + a)! (m - a)! C(l, α - a)`.
declarations.statement: def cgSum (m n k l α : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sum_choose_mul_ite
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_choose_mul_ite {l a α : ℕ} (X : ℝ) :
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (l + 1), (l.choose i : ℝ) * (if α = a + i then X else 0) =
      if a ≤ α then (l.choose (α - a) : ℝ) * X else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_normVec_tmul_vNat
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_normVec_tmul_vNat {α β a i k l : ℕ} (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n)
    (h : α + β = k + l) (hak : a ≤ k) (hil : i ≤ l) :
    tensorForm m n (normVec m α ⊗ₜ normVec n β) (vNat m (a + i) ⊗ₜ vNat n (k - a + (l - i))) =
      if α = a + i then Real.sqrt (normSq m α) * Real.sqrt (normSq n β) else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.tensorForm_normVec_stringVec
declarations.doc: `⟨u_α ⊗ u_β, f^l w_k⟩ = cgSum · √(normSq m α) √(normSq n β)` for `α + β = k + l`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorForm_normVec_stringVec {k l α β : ℕ} (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n)
    (h : α + β = k + l) :
    tensorForm m n (normVec m α ⊗ₜ normVec n β) (stringVec m n k l) =
      cgSum m n k l α * Real.sqrt (normSq m α) * Real.sqrt (normSq n β)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_eq_cgSum
declarations.doc: The Clebsch–Gordan coefficient as one finite sum, with the norm of `w_k` still unevaluated.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_eq_cgSum {k l α β : ℕ} (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n) (h : α + β = k + l) :
    cgCoefficient m n k l α β =
      (Real.sqrt ((normSq (m + n - 2 * k) l : ℝ) * hwNormSq m n k))⁻¹ *
        (cgSum m n k l α * Real.sqrt (normSq m α) * Real.sqrt (normSq n β))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_closed
declarations.doc:
**Closed formula for the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients.** For `α + β = k + l`, with
`N = m + n - 2k`,
`⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ = cgSum · √(normSq m α · normSq n β · (N + 1)! / (normSq N l · hwNormNum))`.
For `α + β ≠ k + l` the coefficient vanishes by `cgCoefficient_eq_zero_of_ne`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_closed {k l α β : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n) (h : α + β = k + l) :
    cgCoefficient m n k l α β = cgSum m n k l α *
      Real.sqrt ((normSq m α : ℝ) * normSq n β * (m + n - 2 * k + 1).factorial /
        ((normSq (m + n - 2 * k) l : ℝ) * hwNormNum m n k))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.zchoose
declarations.doc: `C(n, j)` for `j ≥ 0` and `0` for `j < 0`.
declarations.statement: def zchoose (n : ℕ) (j : ℤ) : ℤ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.zchoose_natCast
declarations.statement: lemma zchoose_natCast (n t : ℕ) : zchoose n t = n.choose t

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.zchoose_of_neg
declarations.statement: lemma zchoose_of_neg {n : ℕ} {j : ℤ} (h : j < 0) : zchoose n j = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.zchoose_succ
declarations.doc: Pascal's rule `C(n + 1, j) = C(n, j) + C(n, j - 1)` for all integers `j`.
declarations.statement: lemma zchoose_succ (n : ℕ) (j : ℤ) : zchoose (n + 1) j = zchoose n j + zchoose n (j - 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sum_range_choose_succ_mul
declarations.doc: Pascal's rule inside a binomial sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_range_choose_succ_mul (f : ℕ → ℤ) (k : ℕ) :
    ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (k + 1 + 1), ((k + 1).choose a : ℤ) * f a =
      ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (k.choose a : ℤ) * f a +
        ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), (k.choose a : ℤ) * f (a + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.racahL
declarations.doc:
`L(k, α, s) = Σ_a (-1)^a C(k, a) C(r + k - a, α - a) C(p + a, s + a)`: the sum `cgSum` after
dividing out factorials.
declarations.statement: def racahL (r p k : ℕ) (α s : ℤ) : ℤ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.racahR
declarations.doc:
`R(k, α, s) = Σ_z (-1)^z C(k, z) C(r, α - z) C(p, s + z)`: Racah's sum after dividing out
factorials.
declarations.statement: def racahR (r p k : ℕ) (α s : ℤ) : ℤ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.racahL_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma racahL_succ (r p k : ℕ) (α s : ℤ) :
    racahL r p (k + 1) α s = racahL r p k α s - racahL r p k (α - 1) (s + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.racahR_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma racahR_succ (r p k : ℕ) (α s : ℤ) :
    racahR r p (k + 1) α s = racahR r p k α s - racahR r p k (α - 1) (s + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.racahL_eq_racahR
declarations.doc:
**The transformation.** `L = R`, by induction on `k`: both satisfy
`X(k + 1, α, s) = X(k, α, s) - X(k, α - 1, s + 1)` and agree for `k = 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma racahL_eq_racahR (r p k : ℕ) (α s : ℤ) : racahL r p k α s = racahR r p k α s

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.racahSum
declarations.doc:
Racah's alternating sum
`Σ_z (-1)^z / (z! (k - z)! (α - z)! (n - β - z)! (m - k - α + z)! (β - k + z)!)`
over the `z` for which all six arguments are nonnegative. In spin notation the arguments are
`z`, `j₁ + j₂ - J - z`, `j₁ - m₁ - z`, `j₂ + m₂ - z`, `J - j₂ + m₁ + z` and `J - j₁ - m₂ + z`.
declarations.statement: def racahSum (m n k α β : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgSum_eq_racahL
declarations.statement:
lemma cgSum_eq_racahL {k l α β : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n)
    (h : α + β = k + l) :
    cgSum m n k l α = (l.factorial : ℝ) * (m - α).factorial * (n - β).factorial *
      (racahL (m - k) (n - k) k α ((l : ℤ) - α) : ℝ)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.racahR_eq_racahSum
declarations.statement:
lemma racahR_eq_racahSum {k l α β : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (h : α + β = k + l) :
    (racahR (m - k) (n - k) k α ((l : ℤ) - α) : ℝ) =
      (k.factorial : ℝ) * (m - k).factorial * (n - k).factorial * racahSum m n k α β

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgSum_eq_racahSum
declarations.doc: `cgSum = l! (m - α)! (n - β)! · k! (m - k)! (n - k)! · racahSum`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgSum_eq_racahSum {k l α β : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n)
    (h : α + β = k + l) :
    cgSum m n k l α = (l.factorial : ℝ) * (m - α).factorial * (n - β).factorial *
      ((k.factorial : ℝ) * (m - k).factorial * (n - k).factorial) * racahSum m n k α β

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_racah
declarations.doc:
**Racah's formula.** For `α + β = k + l`, with `j₁ = m/2`, `m₁ = j₁ - α`, `j₂ = n/2`,
`m₂ = j₂ - β`, `J = (m + n)/2 - k`, `M = J - l`,
`⟨j₁ m₁ j₂ m₂ | J M⟩ = √((2J + 1) (J + j₁ - j₂)! (J - j₁ + j₂)! (j₁ + j₂ - J)! / (j₁ + j₂ + J + 1)!)
  · √((J + M)! (J - M)! (j₁ - m₁)! (j₁ + m₁)! (j₂ - m₂)! (j₂ + m₂)!) · racahSum`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_racah {k l α β : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k) (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n) (h : α + β = k + l) :
    cgCoefficient m n k l α β =
      Real.sqrt (((m + n - 2 * k + 1) * (m - k).factorial * (n - k).factorial * k.factorial : ℕ) /
        ((m + n - k + 1).factorial : ℝ)) *
      Real.sqrt (((m + n - 2 * k - l).factorial * l.factorial * α.factorial * (m - α).factorial *
        β.factorial * (n - β).factorial : ℕ) : ℝ) * racahSum m n k α β

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_add_half_up
declarations.doc:
`⟨j₁ m₁ ½ ½ | j₁ + ½, M⟩ = √((j₁ + M + ½)/(2j₁ + 1))`: with `j₁ = m/2`, `J = j₁ + ½` (`k = 0`),
`M = J - l` and `m₁ = j₁ - l`, the value is `√((m + 1 - l)/(m + 1))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_add_half_up {m l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ m) :
    cgCoefficient m 1 0 l l 0 = Real.sqrt (((m + 1 - l : ℕ) : ℝ) / (m + 1))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_add_half_down
declarations.doc:
`⟨j₁ m₁ ½ -½ | j₁ + ½, M⟩ = √((j₁ - M + ½)/(2j₁ + 1))`: with `j₁ = m/2`, `J = j₁ + ½`
(`k = 0`), `M = J - (l + 1)` and `m₁ = j₁ - l`, the value is `√((l + 1)/(m + 1))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_add_half_down {m l : ℕ} (hl : l ≤ m) :
    cgCoefficient m 1 0 (l + 1) l 1 = Real.sqrt (((l + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (m + 1))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_sub_half_up
declarations.doc:
`⟨j₁ m₁ ½ ½ | j₁ - ½, M⟩ = -√((j₁ - M + ½)/(2j₁ + 1))`: with `j₁ = m/2`, `J = j₁ - ½`
(`k = 1`), `M = J - l` and `m₁ = j₁ - (l + 1)`, the value is `-√((l + 1)/(m + 1))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_sub_half_up {m l : ℕ} (hl : l + 1 ≤ m) :
    cgCoefficient m 1 1 l (l + 1) 0 = -Real.sqrt (((l + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (m + 1))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.cgCoefficient_sub_half_down
declarations.doc:
`⟨j₁ m₁ ½ -½ | j₁ - ½, M⟩ = √((j₁ + M + ½)/(2j₁ + 1))`: with `j₁ = m/2`, `J = j₁ - ½`
(`k = 1`), `M = J - l` and `m₁ = j₁ - l`, the value is `√((m - l)/(m + 1))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cgCoefficient_sub_half_down {m l : ℕ} (hl : l + 1 ≤ m) :
    cgCoefficient m 1 1 l l 1 = Real.sqrt (((m - l : ℕ) : ℝ) / (m + 1))

modules.title: The two coupling schemes of three angular momenta
modules.doc:
The irreducible components of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` as isometric embeddings, the triple tensor product
`V(a) ⊗ V(b) ⊗ V(c)` with its Casimir operator, and the two ways of coupling three angular
momenta.

## i. Overview

Three angular momenta `j₁ = a/2`, `j₂ = b/2`, `j₃ = c/2` live on
`V(a) ⊗ V(b) ⊗ V(c)`. A state of total angular momentum `J` and projection `M` can be built in
two ways:

- `|(j₁ j₂) j₁₂, j₃; J M⟩`: first couple `j₁` and `j₂` to `j₁₂`, then `j₁₂` and `j₃` to `J`;
- `|j₁, (j₂ j₃) j₂₃; J M⟩`: first couple `j₂` and `j₃` to `j₂₃`, then `j₁` and `j₂₃` to `J`.

Both are built from the Clebsch–Gordan states `coupledVec` of `ClebschGordanCoefficients`. The
`k`-th irreducible component of `V(m) ⊗ V(n)` is the image of the isometric embedding
`embed : V(m + n - 2k) → V(m) ⊗ V(n)`, `u_l ↦ |J, J - l⟩`, which intertwines `E`, `F` and `H`
(it is a rescaled inverse of `cgEquiv`). The first scheme is `embed ⊗ 1` applied to the coupled
states of `V(a + b - 2k₁) ⊗ V(c)`, the second is `1 ⊗ embed` followed by the associator.

The recoupling coefficients between the two schemes and the 6j symbols are in `SixJ`.

## ii. Key results

- `embed`, `tensorForm_embed`, `tensorF_embed`: the isometric intertwining embeddings.
- `Triple`, `tripleForm`, `tripleE`, `tripleF`, `tripleH`: the triple tensor product with its
  contravariant form and the total `E`, `F`, `H`.
- `tensorCas`, `tripleCas`: the Casimir operators.
- `stateA`, `stateB`: the two coupling schemes.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The irreducible components as isometric embeddings
- B. The triple tensor product
- C. The Casimir operator
- D. The two coupling schemes

## iv. References

- A. R. Edmonds, *Angular Momentum in Quantum Mechanics*, Princeton University Press (1957),
  chapter 6.

## A. The irreducible components as isometric embeddings

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.embed
declarations.doc:
The isometric embedding `V(m + n - 2k) → V(m) ⊗ V(n)` onto the `k`-th irreducible component,

declarations.statement:

    (w w' : StandardSl2Module ℝ b ⊗[ℝ] StandardSl2Module ℝ c) :
    tripleForm a b c ((TensorProduct.assoc ℝ _ _ _).symm (x ⊗ₜ w))

modules.title: A sum rule for multipole transitions
modules.doc:
`Σ_{μ M_f} ⟨J_i M_i λ μ | J_f M_f⟩² = (2J_f + 1) / (2J_i + 1)`, independent of `M_i`.

## i. Overview

A multipole operator `T^λ_μ` of rank `λ` connects an initial level `J_i` with a final level
`J_f`. By the Wigner–Eckart theorem its matrix elements are
`⟨J_f M_f | T^λ_μ | J_i M_i⟩ = ⟨J_i M_i λ μ | J_f M_f⟩ · ⟨J_f ‖ T^λ ‖ J_i⟩ / √(2J_f + 1)`,
so the total transition rate out of the substate `|J_i M_i⟩`, summed over all final substates and
all components `μ`, is proportional to

`Σ_{μ M_f} ⟨J_i M_i λ μ | J_f M_f⟩² = (2J_f + 1) / (2J_i + 1)`.

The right-hand side does not depend on `M_i`: an unpolarised and a fully polarised initial state
decay at the same total rate, and `|⟨J_f ‖ T^λ ‖ J_i⟩|² / (2J_i + 1)` is the rate of every
substate.

The sum runs over the first and the third column of the Clebsch–Gordan coefficient, which the
orthogonality relations of `ClebschGordanCoefficients` do not cover. It follows from the cyclic
symmetry of the 3j symbols (`threeJR_cycle_columns`), which moves `J_i` into the third column,
and the orthogonality of the 3j symbols.

## ii. Key results

- `wigner3j_cycle`: the cyclic symmetry in the parameters of `ClebschGordanCoefficients`.
- `sum_sq_cgCoefficient_initial`: the sum rule.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The cyclic symmetry
- B. The sum rule

## iv. References

- A. Bohr and B. R. Mottelson, *Nuclear Structure*, Vol. I, Benjamin (1969), appendix 1A.
- A. R. Edmonds, *Angular Momentum in Quantum Mechanics*, Princeton University Press (1957),
  section 5.4.

## A. The cyclic symmetry

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.wigner3j_cycle
declarations.doc:
`(j₁ j₂ J; m₁ m₂ -M) = (j₂ J j₁; m₂ -M m₁)` in the parameters of
`ClebschGordanCoefficients`: the new triple is `(n, m + n - 2k)` with `k' = n - k`, `l' = m - α`,
`α' = β` and `β' = m + n - 2k - l`.
declarations.statement:
lemma wigner3j_cycle {k l α β : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n) (hl : l ≤ m + n - 2 * k)
    (hα : α ≤ m) (hβ : β ≤ n) :
    wigner3j m n k l α β =
      wigner3j n (m + n - 2 * k) (n - k) (m - α) β (m + n - 2 * k - l)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sum_sq_cgCoefficient_initial
declarations.doc:
**Sum rule for multipole transitions.** With `j₁ = m/2 = J_i`, `j₂ = n/2 = λ`,
`J = (m + n)/2 - k = J_f` and `m₁ = j₁ - α = M_i`,
`Σ_{μ M_f} ⟨J_i M_i λ μ | J_f M_f⟩² = (2J_f + 1) / (2J_i + 1)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_sq_cgCoefficient_initial (hmn : 0 < m + n) {k α : ℕ} (hkm : k ≤ m) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (hα : α ≤ m) :
    ∑ b ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (m + n - 2 * k + 1),
      cgCoefficient m n k l α b ^ 2 = ((m + n - 2 * k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)

modules.title: The 9j symbols
modules.doc:
The 9j symbols as sums over products of three 6j symbols, and their invariance under
transposition.

## i. Overview

In doubled units, the 9j symbol
`{j₁₁ j₁₂ j₁₃; j₂₁ j₂₂ j₂₃; j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃}` is
`Σ_J (-1)^J (J + 1) {j₁₁ j₂₁ j₃₁; j₃₂ j₃₃ J} {j₁₂ j₂₂ j₃₂; j₂₁ J j₂₃} {j₁₃ j₂₃ j₃₃; J j₁₁ j₁₂}`
(`nineJSym`), with the 6j symbols `sixJSym` of `SixJSymmetry`. The first 6j symbol contains the
triad `(j₁₁ j₃₃ J)`, so it vanishes for `J > j₁₁ + j₃₃` (`sixJSym_eq_zero_of_lt`) and the sum is
over `J ≤ j₁₁ + j₃₃`. Extending the range does not change it (`nineJSym_eq_sum`).

Transposition of the 3 × 3 array fixes `j₁₁` and `j₃₃`, and hence the range of summation. It
exchanges the first and third 6j symbols and maps the second to itself, up to the tetrahedral
symmetries `sixJSym_swap₁₂`, `sixJSym_swap₂₃`, `sixJSym_flip₁₂`. So the 9j symbol is invariant
under transposition summand by summand (`nineJSym_transpose`).

## ii. Key results

- `nineJSym`: the 9j symbol as a sum over products of three 6j symbols.
- `nineJSym_eq_sum`: the sum may be taken over any larger range.
- `nineJSym_transpose`: invariance under transposition.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The 9j symbol
- B. Invariance under transposition

## iv. References

- NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §34.6, https://dlmf.nist.gov/34.6, equation
  34.6.2, and §34.7, https://dlmf.nist.gov/34.7.
- D. A. Varshalovich, A. N. Moskalev, V. K. Khersonskii, *Quantum Theory of Angular Momentum*,
  World Scientific (1988), chapter 10.

## A. The 9j symbol

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sixJSym_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.doc:
A 6j symbol whose triad `(j₁ j₅ j₆)` violates the triangle inequality `j₆ ≤ j₁ + j₅`
vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma sixJSym_eq_zero_of_lt {j₁ j₂ j₃ j₄ j₅ j₆ : ℕ} (h : j₁ + j₅ < j₆) :
    sixJSym j₁ j₂ j₃ j₄ j₅ j₆ = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.nineJSym
declarations.doc:
The **9j symbol** `{j₁₁ j₁₂ j₁₃; j₂₁ j₂₂ j₂₃; j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃}` (doubled units) as a sum over
products of three 6j symbols.
declarations.statement: def nineJSym (j₁₁ j₁₂ j₁₃ j₂₁ j₂₂ j₂₃ j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃ : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.nineJSym_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The sum defining `nineJSym` may be taken over any range containing `J ≤ j₁₁ + j₃₃`.
declarations.statement:
lemma nineJSym_eq_sum {j₁₁ j₁₂ j₁₃ j₂₁ j₂₂ j₂₃ j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃ N : ℕ} (hN : j₁₁ + j₃₃ < N) :
    nineJSym j₁₁ j₁₂ j₁₃ j₂₁ j₂₂ j₂₃ j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃ =
      ∑ J ∈ Finset.range N, (-1 : ℝ) ^ J * (J + 1) *
        (sixJSym j₁₁ j₂₁ j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃ J * sixJSym j₁₂ j₂₂ j₃₂ j₂₁ J j₂₃ *
          sixJSym j₁₃ j₂₃ j₃₃ J j₁₁ j₁₂)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.nineJSym_transpose
declarations.doc: **Transposition symmetry.** The 9j symbol is invariant under exchange of rows and columns.
declarations.statement:
lemma nineJSym_transpose (j₁₁ j₁₂ j₁₃ j₂₁ j₂₂ j₂₃ j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃ : ℕ) :
    nineJSym j₁₁ j₂₁ j₃₁ j₁₂ j₂₂ j₃₂ j₁₃ j₂₃ j₃₃ =
      nineJSym j₁₁ j₁₂ j₁₃ j₂₁ j₂₂ j₂₃ j₃₁ j₃₂ j₃₃

modules.title: The invariant form and the normalised basis of the standard modules
modules.doc:
The contravariant form on `V(n)` and the orthonormal basis `|j, m⟩` with the textbook matrix
elements of `J₊`, `J₋` and `Jz`.

## i. Overview

The basis `v_a = f^a v_0` of `V(n)` used throughout is not normalised. There is a symmetric
bilinear form on `V(n)`, unique up to a scalar, for which the raising and lowering operators are
adjoint and the weight operator is symmetric:
`⟨e x, y⟩ = ⟨x, f y⟩`, `⟨h x, y⟩ = ⟨x, h y⟩`. In the basis `v_a` it is diagonal with
`⟨v_a, v_a⟩ = a! · n!/(n - a)!`.

Over `ℝ` the rescaled vectors `u_a = v_a / √⟨v_a, v_a⟩` are orthonormal. With `j = n/2` and
`m = j - a` they are the states `|j, m⟩`, and the operators act by the textbook formulas
(Condon–Shortley phases):

- `J₊ |j, m⟩ = √((j - m)(j + m + 1)) |j, m + 1⟩`, i.e. `e u_{a+1} = √((a+1)(n-a)) u_a`;
- `J₋ |j, m⟩ = √((j + m)(j - m + 1)) |j, m - 1⟩`, i.e. `f u_a = √((a+1)(n-a)) u_{a+1}`;
- `2Jz |j, m⟩ = 2m |j, m⟩`, i.e. `h u_a = (n - 2a) u_a`.

## ii. Key results

- `normSq` is `⟨v_a, v_a⟩` and `invForm` the contravariant form.
- `invForm_comp_ρE` and `invForm_comp_ρH` express that `e, f` are adjoint and `h` is symmetric.
- `normVec` is the normalised basis over `ℝ`; `invForm_normVec` is orthonormality.
- `ρE_normVec_succ`, `ρF_normVec` and `ρH_normVec` are the textbook matrix elements.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The contravariant form
  - A.1. Squared norms
  - A.2. Definition and values
  - A.3. Contravariance
- B. The normalised basis over ℝ

## iv. References

- J. J. Sakurai and J. Napolitano, *Modern Quantum Mechanics*, 3rd ed., Cambridge University
  Press (2020), section 3.5.

## A. The contravariant form

### A.1. Squared norms

sections.text: ## B. The normalised basis over ℝ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.normSq
declarations.doc: The squared norm `⟨v_a, v_a⟩ = a! · n!/(n - a)!` of the basis vector `v_a` of `V(n)`.
declarations.statement: def normSq (n a : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.normSq_succ
declarations.statement: lemma normSq_succ (n a : ℕ) : normSq n (a + 1) = normSq n a * ((a + 1) * (n - a))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.normSq_pos
declarations.statement: lemma normSq_pos {n a : ℕ} (ha : a ≤ n) : 0 < normSq n a

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm
declarations.doc: The contravariant form on `V(n)`: diagonal in the basis `v_a` with entries `normSq n a`.
declarations.statement: def invForm : StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] K

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_v
declarations.statement:
lemma invForm_v (i j : Fin (n + 1)) :
    invForm K n (v i) (v j) = if i = j then (normSq n i : K) else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_vNat
declarations.statement:
lemma invForm_vNat (a b : ℕ) :
    invForm K n (vNat n a) (vNat n b) = if a = b ∧ a ≤ n then (normSq n a : K) else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.bilin_ext_vNat
declarations.doc: Two bilinear forms on `V(n)` agree if they agree on all pairs `v_a, v_b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bilin_ext_vNat {B B' : StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] K}
    (h : ∀ a b, B (vNat n a) (vNat n b) = B' (vNat n a) (vNat n b)) : B = B'

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_comp_ρE
declarations.doc: The raising and lowering operators are adjoint: `⟨e x, y⟩ = ⟨x, f y⟩`.
declarations.statement: lemma invForm_comp_ρE : (invForm K n).comp ρE = (invForm K n).compl₂ ρF

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_comp_ρH
declarations.doc: The weight operator is symmetric: `⟨h x, y⟩ = ⟨x, h y⟩`.
declarations.statement: lemma invForm_comp_ρH : (invForm K n).comp ρH = (invForm K n).compl₂ ρH

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_comm
declarations.doc: The form is symmetric.
declarations.statement: lemma invForm_comm (x y : StandardSl2Module K n) : invForm K n x y = invForm K n y x

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.normVec
declarations.doc:
The normalised basis vector `u_a = v_a / √(normSq n a)` of `V(n)` over `ℝ`; for `a ≤ n` it
is the state `|j, m⟩` with `j = n/2`, `m = j - a`.
declarations.statement: def normVec (n a : ℕ) : StandardSl2Module ℝ n

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sqrt_normSq_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma sqrt_normSq_succ (n a : ℕ) :
    Real.sqrt (normSq n (a + 1)) =
      Real.sqrt (normSq n a) * Real.sqrt (((a : ℝ) + 1) * ((n : ℝ) - a))

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.invForm_normVec
declarations.doc: Orthonormality: `⟨u_a, u_b⟩ = δ_ab` for `a, b ≤ n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invForm_normVec {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≤ n) (hb : b ≤ n) :
    invForm ℝ n (normVec n a) (normVec n b) = if a = b then 1 else 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_normVec
declarations.doc:
The weight operator on the normalised basis: `h u_a = (n - 2a) u_a`, i.e.
`Jz |j, m⟩ = m |j, m⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ρH_normVec (a : ℕ) :
    (ρH : Module.End ℝ (StandardSl2Module ℝ n)) (normVec n a) =
      ((n : ℝ) - 2 * a) • normVec n a

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρF_normVec
declarations.doc:
The lowering operator on the normalised basis: `f u_a = √((a+1)(n-a)) u_{a+1}` for `a < n`,
i.e. `J₋ |j, m⟩ = √((j + m)(j - m + 1)) |j, m - 1⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ρF_normVec {a : ℕ} (ha : a < n) :
    (ρF : Module.End ℝ (StandardSl2Module ℝ n)) (normVec n a) =
      Real.sqrt (((a : ℝ) + 1) * ((n : ℝ) - a)) • normVec n (a + 1)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_normVec_succ
declarations.doc:
The raising operator on the normalised basis: `e u_{a+1} = √((a+1)(n-a)) u_a` for `a < n`,
i.e. `J₊ |j, m⟩ = √((j - m)(j + m + 1)) |j, m + 1⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ρE_normVec_succ {a : ℕ} (ha : a < n) :
    (ρE : Module.End ℝ (StandardSl2Module ℝ n)) (normVec n (a + 1)) =
      Real.sqrt (((a : ℝ) + 1) * ((n : ℝ) - a)) • normVec n a

modules.title: The projection theorem for vector operators
modules.doc:
Tensor operators are unique up to a scalar, and every vector operator on an irreducible
multiplet is a multiple of the angular momentum itself.

## i. Overview

By the Wigner–Eckart theorem the tensor operators of rank `k` from `V(m)` to `V(p)` form a space
of dimension at most one. So if one nonzero tensor operator is known, every other one is a scalar
multiple of it.

For rank `k = 2` (vector operators, `κ = 1` in physics notation) and `m = p = n` there is a
canonical nonzero tensor operator: the `sl₂` action itself, `v_0 ↦ e`, `v_1 ↦ -h`, `v_2 ↦ -2f`,
corresponding to the spherical components of the angular momentum `J`. Hence every vector
operator `T` on the multiplet `V(n)` satisfies `T = c • J` for a single scalar `c`. This is the
projection theorem behind the Landé `g`-factor; the usual formula
`c = ⟨J · V⟩ / (j(j+1))` for the scalar is not part of this file.

## ii. Key results

- `IsTensorIntertwiner.exists_eq_smul_of_ne_zero` and `IsTensorOperator.exists_eq_smul_of_ne_zero`
  give uniqueness up to a scalar.
- `sl2Operator` is the `sl₂` action as a rank-2 tensor operator, see `isTensorOperator_sl2Operator`.
- `IsTensorOperator.exists_eq_smul_sl2Operator` is the projection theorem.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Uniqueness up to a scalar
- B. The angular momentum as a vector operator
  - B.1. Definition and values
  - B.2. Commutation relations
- C. The projection theorem

## iv. References

- J. J. Sakurai and J. Napolitano, *Modern Quantum Mechanics*, 3rd ed., Cambridge University
  Press (2020), section 3.11.

## A. Uniqueness up to a scalar

sections.text:
## B. The angular momentum as a vector operator

### B.1. Definition and values

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.IsTensorIntertwiner.exists_eq_smul_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
Two tensor intertwiners into the same `V(p)` are proportional, provided the second one is
nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsTensorIntertwiner.exists_eq_smul_of_ne_zero (hmn : 0 < m + n)
    {φ ψ : StandardSl2Module K m ⊗[K] StandardSl2Module K n →ₗ[K] StandardSl2Module K p}

Two tensor operators of rank `k` from `V(m)` to `V(p)` are proportional, provided the second

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sl2Operator
declarations.doc:
The `sl₂` action on `V(n)` as a tensor operator of rank 2: `v_0 ↦ e`, `v_1 ↦ -h`,
`v_2 ↦ -2f`. These are the spherical components of the angular momentum, up to normalisation.
declarations.statement: def sl2Operator : StandardSl2Module K 2 →ₗ[K] Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sl2Operator_vNat_zero
declarations.statement: lemma sl2Operator_vNat_zero : sl2Operator (K := K) n (vNat 2 0) = ρE

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sl2Operator_vNat_one
declarations.statement: lemma sl2Operator_vNat_one : sl2Operator (K := K) n (vNat 2 1) = (-1 : K) • ρH

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sl2Operator_vNat_two
declarations.statement: lemma sl2Operator_vNat_two : sl2Operator (K := K) n (vNat 2 2) = (-2 : K) • ρF

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sl2Operator_vNat_of_lt
declarations.statement: lemma sl2Operator_vNat_of_lt {l : ℕ} (hl : 2 < l) : sl2Operator (K := K) n (vNat 2 l) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_mul_ρF'
declarations.statement: lemma ρE_mul_ρF' : (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) * ρF = ρF * ρE + ρH

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_mul_ρE'
declarations.statement: lemma ρH_mul_ρE' : (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) * ρE = ρE * ρH + (2 : K) • ρE

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_mul_ρF'
declarations.statement: lemma ρH_mul_ρF' : (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K n)) * ρF = ρF * ρH - (2 : K) • ρF

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_vNat_two_one
declarations.statement:
lemma ρE_vNat_two_one : (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K 2)) (vNat 2 1) =
    (2 : K) • vNat 2 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρE_vNat_two_two
declarations.statement:
lemma ρE_vNat_two_two : (ρE : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K 2)) (vNat 2 2) =
    (2 : K) • vNat 2 1

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_vNat_two_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma ρH_vNat_two_zero : (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K 2)) (vNat 2 0) =
    (2 : K) • vNat 2 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_vNat_two_one
declarations.statement: lemma ρH_vNat_two_one : (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K 2)) (vNat 2 1) = 0

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.ρH_vNat_two_two
declarations.statement:
lemma ρH_vNat_two_two : (ρH : Module.End K (StandardSl2Module K 2)) (vNat 2 2) =
    (-2 : K) • vNat 2 2

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.comm_of_vNat
declarations.doc:
A commutation relation `[Y, A x] = A (X x)` for a linear `A` holds for all `x` once it holds
on the coordinate vectors.

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.isTensorOperator_sl2Operator
declarations.doc: The `sl₂` action is a tensor operator of rank 2 on every `V(n)`.
declarations.statement: lemma isTensorOperator_sl2Operator : IsTensorOperator (sl2Operator (K := K) n)

declarations.name: PhyslibAlpha.Sl2.sl2Operator_ne_zero
declarations.doc: On `V(n)` with `n > 0` the `sl₂` action is a nonzero tensor operator.
declarations.statement: lemma sl2Operator_ne_zero (hn : 0 < n) : sl2Operator (K := K) n ≠ 0

declarations.doc:
**Projection theorem.** Every vector operator (tensor operator of rank 2) on the multiplet
